# An interval split at its midpoint, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_split_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Two intervals that together are $X = [x_l, x_u]$, split at a point of it:

$$X = [a_l, a_u] \cup [b_l, b_u].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $a_l = a_{l0} + a_{l1}$, $a_u = a_{u0} + a_{u1}$, $b_l = b_{l0} + b_{l1}$, $b_u = b_{u0} + b_{u1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call its core, [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md) and [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md), instead.

## Requires

- $[x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $[a_l, a_u]$ and $[b_l, b_u]$ are canonical intervals.
- If $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is empty, both are.
- Otherwise neither is, $a_l = x_l$, $b_u = x_u$ and $a_u = b_l$: the two together are $X$, split at that point, which is in $X$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_split_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_split_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_split_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds and the midpoint of interval_mid_rad_2, moved into the interval (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_split_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_split_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md), [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# An interval with 2-limb bounds split at its midpoint (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", the
# row of split() and "The empty set and the whole line"): [xl, m] and [m, xu], m the midpoint of
# interval_mid_rad_2, which is in [xl, xu]; their union is the interval. The whole line gives [-inf,
# 0] and [0, +inf], a half-line [l, +inf] gives [l, Omega] and [Omega, +inf] (when l is not beyond
# Omega: see the step below), and the empty set the empty set twice. One step more than for one limb: a bound of two limbs can be beyond Omega (Omega plus less than half a
# gap), and the midpoint +-Omega of a half-line is then outside the interval; the point of the split
# is the midpoint moved into [xl, xu] by lt_2_2, the bound itself in that case. The midpoint is
# computed by the steps of interval_mid_rad_2 that make it, without its radius: interval_mid_rad_2 is
# not called, since the radius would be unused (compilers remove its fused operations, which the
# object-code check counts), and the empty set is told by the lower bound, +inf.

om         = pred(const inf)
mo         = neg(om)
ml         = lt(xl0, mo)
l0         = select(ml, mo, xl0)
l1         = select(ml, 0, xl1)
mu         = lt(om, xu0)
h0         = select(mu, om, xu0)
h1         = select(mu, 0, xu1)
(hl0, hl1) = mul_pow2_2(l0, l1, const up(1/2))
(hu0, hu1) = mul_pow2_2(h0, h1, const up(1/2))
(ma0, ma1) = add_2_2(hl0, hl1, hu0, hu1)
ca         = lt_2_2(ma0, ma1, l0, l1)
mb0        = select(ca, l0, ma0)
mb1        = select(ca, l1, ma1)
cb         = lt_2_2(h0, h1, mb0, mb1)
mc0        = select(cb, h0, mb0)
mc1        = select(cb, h1, mb1)
md0        = select(ml, mo, mc0)
md1        = select(ml, 0, mc1)
me0        = select(mu, om, md0)
me1        = select(mu, 0, md1)
bo         = and(ml, mu)
m0         = select(bo, 0, me0)
m1         = select(bo, 0, me1)
ka         = lt_2_2(m0, m1, xl0, xl1)
n0         = select(ka, xl0, m0)
n1         = select(ka, xl1, m1)
kb         = lt_2_2(xu0, xu1, n0, n1)
p0         = select(kb, xu0, n0)
p1         = select(kb, xu1, n1)
ne         = lt(xl0, const inf)
mi         = neg(const inf)
al0        = copy(xl0)
al1        = copy(xl1)
au0        = select(ne, p0, mi)
au1        = select(ne, p1, 0)
bl0        = select(ne, p0, const inf)
bl1        = select(ne, p1, 0)
bu0        = copy(xu0)
bu1        = copy(xu1)
```
